title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
author: Aesop
source: Public domain. Retold from Aesop's Fables.

pages.text: Once upon a time, there was a shepherd boy who watched over a flock of sheep on a hillside near his village. All day long he sat under a tree, and all day long the sheep nibbled the grass. The boy thought it was very, very boring.
One afternoon, the boy had an idea for a trick. He jumped up, cupped his hands around his mouth, and shouted down to the village, "Wolf! Wolf! A wolf is chasing the sheep!"

The villagers dropped everything and came running up the hill to help. But when they arrived, there was no wolf at all — only the boy, laughing and laughing. "There is no wolf!" he giggled. "I fooled you all!" The villagers grumbled and walked back down the hill.

A few days later, the boy grew bored again. "Wolf! Wolf!" he shouted, even louder than before. Once more the villagers came running, and once more they found the boy laughing at his trick. "You should not cry wolf when there is no wolf," they warned him, and they went back to their work.

Then, one evening as the sun was setting, a real wolf crept out of the forest. The sheep bleated and scattered in fear. The boy leapt to his feet. "Wolf! Wolf!" he cried with all his might. "Please, help! A real wolf!"
But down in the village, the people only shook their heads. "He is trying to fool us again," they said, and nobody came. The wolf scattered the whole flock before loping back into the woods.

The next morning, the boy sadly told the villagers what had truly happened. A kind old farmer put a hand on his shoulder and said, "Nobody believes someone who tells lies — even when they are telling the truth." And from that day on, the boy only ever called for help when he really needed it.
